subject: Interim rate adjudication & fairness carve-out request — Catalyst Health pilot
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@catalysthealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@catalysthealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term rate uplift + fairness carve-out for pilot weekend

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot is moving fast on our side. We have a coordinated customer event on Nov 12-13 where we expect a concentrated burst: a set of 8 physician-facing workflows will call the patient-summary generation route concurrently. Our ops team projects a 6x spike in tokens/sec for a ~36-hour window during the event (attached projection).

As we discussed, Catalyst Health needs a temporary adjustment to the default fairness and burst ceilings so responses remain sub-500ms P95 and we don't see throttled completions mid-session. Specifically we're requesting:
- A temporary burst ceiling increase from 500k tokens/min to 2.5M tokens/min for the window Nov 12 08:00 UTC — Nov 13 20:00 UTC
- A short-lived priority lane allowing up to 15% of regional capacity for our tenant (tagged pilot:catalyst)

We understand this is exceptional and are happy to accept limited duration, monitoring hooks, and a cost premium for the uplift. Attached: traffic projection + SOC2 summary.

Can you (1) confirm whether Redwood can approve a temporary carve-out under the Dedicated/fairness policy, and (2) what information you need from procurement/engineering to evaluate the impact?

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Integrations, Catalyst Health
elena@catalysthealth.com

Attachments: CatalystHealth_traffic_projection_Q4.pdf (pdf, 480KB) | SOC2-ready-security-summary.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term rate uplift + fairness carve-out for pilot weekend

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the projection file. Looping in Lauren (AM) and Rishi (SRE/Capacity) so we can scope the operational risk. Quick notes from my side:

- We can consider an interim carve-out, but it needs to be tightly scoped: exact start/end times (including timezone) + a fall-back plan if regional latency exceeds our SLOs.
- Technical options we can propose: a) temporary token-burst window assigned to a tagged priority pool, b) temporary route-level rate override with strict per-request timeouts, or c) short-lived dedicated job (reserved pods) for the traffic window.
- Our fairness policy is conservative to protect multi-tenant P95 latency; a 2.5M tokens/min cap will require an explicit approval from Capacity and Product. Rishi — can you confirm whether the priority pool (15%) is feasible for the us-west region for the proposed window?

Action items I propose:
1) Elena to confirm final UTC window and peak concurrency (sessions/min and avg tokens/session).
2) Catalyst signs an acknowledgement for an elevated runbook: extra monitoring, cost uplift, and immediate mitigation triggers (auto-failover to secondary model if latency>350ms P95 for >5m).
3) Internal: Capacity to run an emergency readiness check and provide an approval decision by Oct 5 EOD.

If you prefer, we can do a short call Fri morning to walk through specifics.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
